note: dateChecked is set only for sources whose URL and cited claim were checked on that date. null = cited from prior knowledge and not re-verified; treat accordingly.

w3c-fp-guidance.title: Mitigating Browser Fingerprinting in Web Specifications
w3c-fp-guidance.supports: Definitions of passive/active fingerprinting, entropy, and mitigation principles for spec authors.

mdn-client-hints.title: HTTP Client hints
mdn-client-hints.supports: Client Hint request headers and the Accept-CH opt-in mechanism.

mdn-uach.title: User-Agent Client Hints API
mdn-uach.supports: navigator.userAgentData low- and high-entropy values; browser support.

mdn-audiocontext.title: AudioContext
mdn-audiocontext.supports: Web Audio API processing graph used by the offline audio test.

mdn-canvas.title: Canvas API
mdn-canvas.supports: 2D canvas drawing and pixel read-back APIs.

mdn-webgl-debug.title: WEBGL_debug_renderer_info extension
mdn-webgl-debug.supports: Unmasked vendor/renderer strings and their privacy implications.

eff-cyt-about.title: About Cover Your Tracks
eff-cyt-about.supports: Lists measured characteristics (user agent, Accept headers, screen, timezone, fonts, canvas and WebGL hashes, DNT, platform, language, touch) and that uniqueness is computed against a database of recently observed visitors.

eckersley-2010.title: How Unique Is Your Web Browser? (Eckersley, PETS 2010)
eckersley-2010.supports: 83.6% of 470,161 sampled browsers had a unique fingerprint. Table 2, mean surprisal per variable in isolation: user agent 10.0 bits, plugins 15.4, fonts 13.9, video (screen) 4.83, supercookies 2.12, HTTP accept 6.09, timezone 3.04, cookies enabled 0.353.

laperdrix-2016.title: Beauty and the Beast: Diverting modern web browsers to build unique browser fingerprints (IEEE S&P 2016)
laperdrix-2016.supports: 118,934 fingerprints from AmIUnique; canvas is highly discriminating; mobile fingerprinting is as effective as desktop.

gomezboix-2018.title: Hiding in the Crowd: an Analysis of the Effectiveness of Browser Fingerprinting at Large Scale (WWW 2018)
gomezboix-2018.supports: On ~2 million fingerprints from a large French site, only 33.6% were unique, far lower than self-selected datasets. Shows population bias in uniqueness claims.

acar-2014.title: The Web Never Forgets: Persistent Tracking Mechanisms in the Wild (ACM CCS 2014)
acar-2014.supports: First large-scale study of canvas fingerprinting (over 5% of top 100k sites), evercookies/respawning and cookie syncing. Press coverage attributes ~95% of canvas scripts to AddThis.

englehardt-2016.title: Online Tracking: A 1-million-site Measurement and Analysis (ACM CCS 2016)
englehardt-2016.supports: Canvas fingerprinting on 14,371 sites from ~400 script domains; discovery of AudioContext fingerprinting in the wild; WebRTC and Battery API fingerprinting.

iqbal-2021.title: Fingerprinting the Fingerprinters: Learning to Detect Browser Fingerprinting Behaviors (IEEE S&P 2021)
iqbal-2021.supports: Machine-learning detection of fingerprinting scripts in the wild.

cao-2017.title: (Cross-)Browser Fingerprinting via OS and Hardware Level Features (NDSS 2017)
cao-2017.supports: WebGL rendering tasks that identify devices across browsers.

drawnapart-2022.title: DRAWNAPART: A Device Identification Technique based on Remote GPU Fingerprinting (NDSS 2022)
drawnapart-2022.supports: GPU execution-timing differences distinguish devices with identical GPU models.

olejnik-2015.title: The leaking battery: A privacy analysis of the HTML5 Battery Status API
olejnik-2015.supports: Battery level and discharge time can act as a short-term cross-site identifier.

solomos-2021.title: Tales of Favicons and Caches: Persistent Tracking in Modern Browsers (NDSS 2021)
solomos-2021.supports: Favicon cache used as a persistent identifier surviving incognito and cookie clearing.

cloak-2016.title: Cloak of Visibility: Detecting When Machines Browse a Different Web (IEEE S&P 2016)
cloak-2016.supports: Underground cloaking services fingerprint visitors (IP, user agent, browser properties) to hide malicious content from security crawlers.

fpjs-sources.title: FingerprintJS open-source entropy sources (src/sources)
fpjs-sources.supports: Source modules include: apple_pay, architecture, audio, audio_base_latency, canvas, color_depth, color_gamut, contrast, cookies_enabled, date_time_locale, device_memory, dom_blockers, font_preferences, fonts, forced_colors, hardware_concurrency, hdr, indexed_db, inverted_colors, languages, local_storage, math, monochrome, os_cpu, pdf_viewer_enabled, platform, plugins, private_click_measurement, reduced_motion, reduced_transparency, screen_frame, screen_resolution, session_storage, timezone, touch_support, user_agent_data, vendor, vendor_flavors, webgl.

cf-ja3.title: JA3/JA4 fingerprint
cf-ja3.supports: "JA3 and JA4 fingerprints identify TLS clients based on how they initiate connections." Available to Bot Management Enterprise customers.

cf-turnstile.title: Turnstile widget modes
cf-turnstile.supports: Managed mode "chooses the appropriate action based on client-side signals and risk levels"; challenges run in the visitor's browser. Specific signals are not listed.

datadome-cdp.title: How New Headless Chrome & the CDP Signal Are Impacting Bot Detection
datadome-cdp.supports: Describes detecting Chrome DevTools Protocol usage and headless Chrome; notes navigator.webdriver can be hidden by disabling AutomationControlled.

akamai-h2.title: Passive Fingerprinting of HTTP/2 Clients (Black Hat Europe 2017)
akamai-h2.supports: HTTP/2 SETTINGS, WINDOW_UPDATE, PRIORITY and pseudo-header order form a passive client fingerprint; based on >10M connections.

ja4.title: JA4+ network fingerprinting
ja4.supports: JA4 TLS client fingerprint format and related JA4+ methods.

p0f.title: p0f v3 passive OS fingerprinting
p0f.supports: Passive TCP/IP stack fingerprinting (TTL, window size, options).

localmess.title: Local Mess: covert web-to-app tracking via localhost on Android
localmess.publisher: Researchers (Radboud University, IMDEA Networks et al.)
localmess.supports: Meta Pixel sent the _fbp cookie to Facebook/Instagram apps via WebRTC STUN/TURN to localhost ports 12580–12591; Yandex Metrica used localhost HTTP(S). Disclosed June 2025; Meta stopped on June 3, 2025.

nullsweep-portscan.title: Why is This Website Port Scanning me?
nullsweep-portscan.supports: eBay's check.js (served via a CNAME to online-metrix.net, ThreatMetrix) probed localhost ports for remote-desktop software over WebSockets (May 2020).

register-ebay.title: eBay port scans your PC
register-ebay.supports: Press coverage of the eBay / ThreatMetrix localhost scan.

olejnik-google-2024.title: Biggest privacy erosion in 10 years? On Google's policy change towards fingerprinting
olejnik-google-2024.supports: Google announced in December 2024 that its ad platform policies would permit fingerprinting/IP-based techniques from February 16, 2025.

chromium-ua-reduction.title: User-Agent Reduction
chromium-ua-reduction.supports: Chrome freezes/reduces OS and device details in the User-Agent string; detailed values move to Client Hints.

tor-manual-fp.title: Understanding browser fingerprinting (Tor Browser manual)
tor-manual-fp.supports: Uniformity strategy; letterboxing (window sizes in 200×100 multiples); font enumeration limits; canvas extraction blocking; limited languages; user-agent normalization.

brave-fp2.title: Fingerprinting defenses 2.0
brave-fp2.supports: "Farbling" randomizes canvas and Web Audio output with a per-session, per-eTLD+1 seed.

mozilla-rfp.title: Resist Fingerprinting
mozilla-rfp.supports: Mozilla recommends Fingerprinting Protection (FPP) in Enhanced Tracking Protection for most users; privacy.resistFingerprinting is stricter and may break sites.

mozilla-fpp-wiki.title: Fingerprinting (Firefox Fingerprinting Protection deployment)
mozilla-fpp-wiki.supports: Tracks deployment of Firefox Fingerprinting Protection (FPP) protections.

webkit-tp.title: Tracking Prevention in WebKit
webkit-tp.supports: Web content sees only web fonts and OS-bundled fonts (not user-installed); user agent frozen across minor updates; other anti-fingerprinting measures.

webkit-pb2.title: Private Browsing 2.0
webkit-pb2.supports: Safari 17 Advanced Fingerprinting Protection, including noise added to fingerprintable web APIs in Private Browsing.

guardian-tor-stinks.title: 'Tor Stinks' presentation
guardian-tor-stinks.supports: Leaked NSA slides discuss de-anonymising Tor users, including via evercookie-style persistent identifiers.

ayenson-2011.title: Flash Cookies and Privacy II: Now with HTML5 and ETag Respawning
ayenson-2011.supports: Documented ETag-based and HTML5-storage respawning, including by KISSmetrics.

fpjs-architecture.title: FingerprintJS architecture source (src/sources/architecture.ts)
fpjs-architecture.supports: Computes Infinity − Infinity in a Float32Array and reads the most significant byte: x86/x86-64 produce a NaN with the sign bit set, distinguishing them from other CPU architectures.

cascading-spy-sheets-2025.title: Cascading Spy Sheets: Exploiting the Complexity of Modern CSS for Email and Browser Fingerprinting (NDSS 2025)
cascading-spy-sheets-2025.supports: Script-less fingerprinting with CSS distinguished 1152 of 1176 (97.95%) tested browser-OS combinations without JavaScript.

imc-2025-canvas.title: Characterizing Canvas Fingerprinting Use Across the Web (IMC 2025)
imc-2025-canvas.publisher: Luo, Ritter, Savage, Voelker (UC San Diego)
imc-2025-canvas.supports: Measures how canvas fingerprinting services are deployed across the web.

popets-2025-behavior.title: Rethinking Fingerprinting: An Assessment of Behavior-based Methods (PoPETs 2025)
popets-2025-behavior.supports: Examines how behavioral and browser fingerprinting can be combined for more effective linking.

popets-2025-demographics.title: How Unique is Whose Web Browser? The Role of Demographics in Browser Fingerprinting (PoPETs 2025)
popets-2025-demographics.supports: Browser attributes commonly collected for fingerprinting can be used to predict demographics with machine learning.

beyond-the-crawl-2025.title: Beyond the Crawl: Unmasking Browser Fingerprinting in Real User Interactions
beyond-the-crawl-2025.supports: Automated crawls miss almost half (45%) of the fingerprinting websites encountered by real users.

creepjs.title: CreepJS
creepjs.supports: Open-source research tool that detects API tampering ("lies"), fingerprints extension code and privacy settings, and probes new high-entropy APIs, including comparing worker and main-thread values.
